args.title: checkout-api v2.3.1 failing health checks — rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary: After the deploy of checkout-api v2.3.1 to production, the service failed health checks in all regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) with an error rate of 18%. v2.3.1-rc had also been unhealthy in staging. Action taken: rolled checkout-api back in all production regions to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production. After the rollback, all regions run v2.3.0, the service is healthy, and the error rate is 0.2%. Follow-up: find the root cause of the v2.3.1 failure before redeploying, and check why a release that was unhealthy in staging was promoted.

trace.final:
I rolled checkout-api back to v2.3.0, and it's healthy again in all regions. The SEV2 incident is open as INC-0001, and the on-call engineer has been paged.

- **Problem:** The latest deploy, v2.3.1, was failing health checks in us-east, us-west and eu-west, with an 18% error rate.
- **Rollback:** v2.3.0 is the most recent release that was healthy in production, so I rolled back to it in all three regions. Since that version has run healthy in production before, it didn't need change-manager approval. After the rollback, the error rate is 0.2%.
- **Incident:** INC-0001 describes the failure, the rollback and the follow-ups below.

**Follow-ups noted in the incident:**
- Find the root cause before redeploying v2.3.1.
- Find out why v2.3.1 was promoted to production when its release candidate (v2.3.1-rc) had already failed health checks in staging.
